operation_tail.detail: The official Spring 2026 page remains a 13 May 2026 publication describing fixed broadband availability as of January 2026.
The Spring update reports availability from fixed-line and fixed-wireless-access networks and is not treated as measured parcel throughput.
Headline gigabit-capable and full-fibre coverage figures focus on residential properties and are not applied to commercial parcel rows.
Full-fibre take-up is reported for residential and commercial premises combined and remains separate from residential coverage availability.
Premises without decent broadband are reported for residential and commercial premises combined and are not substituted for postcode coverage fields.
The official interactive report contains latest and historical data; historical snapshots are not merged into January 2026 candidate values.
Ofcom uses the collection to update coverage checkers, but checker output is not accepted as the corrected versioned r2 archive.
The Spring 2026 download section explicitly links licence conditions through Ofcom's terms of use.
Ofcom permits reproduction when material is reproduced accurately and is not used in a misleading context.
Reused Ofcom material must acknowledge Ofcom copyright and specify the document or publication title.
The Ofcom logo is excluded from ordinary reproduction permissions and is not bundled into data reuse.
Ofcom states that website material is provided as-is without guarantees of currency or accuracy, so snapshot and binary readback evidence remain mandatory.
Ofcom states it is committed to making public-sector information available for reuse where possible.
ONS permits commercial or private reuse under the Open Government Licence without a specific application, subject to licence conditions.
ONS requires source accreditation when ONS content is reproduced.
ONS warns that some geography products include third-party intellectual-property rights requiring the appropriate attribution statements.
ONS postcode products derived from Code-Point Open are supplied under the Open Government Licence.
Commercial reuse of Northern Ireland BT postcodes requires a separate Land and Property Services licence; this does not affect the England shard.
Postcode reuse requires the applicable OS, Royal Mail and ONS attribution statements.
ONSPD supports direct mapping by postcode grid reference while NSPL uses Output Area and best-fit statistical geography; the methods are not interchanged.
ONSPD links both current and terminated UK postcodes to geographic areas.
A postcode straddling a boundary is assigned using the mean grid reference of its addresses, not every covered address or parcel.
The one-metre grid-reference product resolution does not make a postcode centroid an exact premise or parcel coordinate.
ONS postcode products are released quarterly in February, May, August and November, so release vintage remains explicit.
ONS CSV postcode products use comma-delimited variable records, double-quoted text and field headings; parsers must preserve that structure.
ONS states that a blank DOTERM field identifies a current postcode.
ONS states that a populated DOTERM date identifies a terminated postcode and keeps the row review-only.
ONS separately provides a postcode centroids product containing only live postcodes; it is not substituted for the full ONSPD lifecycle directory.
ONS describes ONSPD as mapping by postcode centre and NSPL as statistical linkage through Output Areas.
Once a postcode is assigned to an Output Area in NSPL, that linkage is retained for statistical use and is not treated as direct parcel geometry.
ONSPD supplies the district based on the postcode grid reference, while NSPL supplies a best-fit district based on the 2021 Output Area.
ONS cautions that Excel may be unsuitable for large postcode directories; validation must use tooling that preserves all rows and columns.
Visual inspection of page 1 confirms the 7 July 2026 v2 correction, CW/CV and MK/ME duplicate fixes and renaming of all 121 all-premises postcode files to r2.
Visual inspection of page 4 confirms 121 all-premises r2 files with 1,741,096 rows and the separate residential r1 set.
Visual inspection of pages 4 and 5 confirms postcode identity fields, percentage availability fields and exclusion of premise-count fields from postcode files.
Thirty-six official licensing, attribution, lifecycle, product-selection and visual-PDF controls were published line by line; candidate counts remain unchanged pending exact r2 bytes.
